President Trump is blaming the Biden administration for outdated air traffic
control equipment and urging Congress to fund a replacement.
Republicans have controlled both Congress and the White House since January of 2025.
The president's comments on social media come two days after radar and communications
problems triggered an hours-long nationwide ground stop.
Passengers are still facing cancellations and delays as airlines
work to get planes and crews back in position.
Steve Feiderman reports from Los Angeles International Airport.
Even though things are improving, many flights continue to be canceled or delayed.
Yesterday was another difficult day for travelers, not as bad as Friday,
but according to the website FlightAware, thousands of flights were still impacted.
At Los Angeles International, Marilyn Mathis and her husband spent much of the day trying to get
home to Houston. Like many others, she tried to come up with ways to sleep at the airport.
I'm sleeping on the floor, sitting on your suitcases, head up against the wall.
How was that?
Not good. Not good.
Federal officials say they hope to have things back to normal by Sunday night,
but there could be residual effects for a few additional days.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Feiderman in Los Angeles.
President Trump will travel to the Philippines on Tuesday for talks with Southeast Asian leaders.
Diane Desierto is a professor of law and global affairs at the University of Notre Dame.
She says Trump's attendance could help reassure leaders about U.S. support for the region.
The visit is extremely important to give it that kind of commitment, but also, I think,
as part of assurances given the amount of investment that is up for decision-making at the summit.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations opened today in Manila.
Israel says it's killed a top Hamas commander in southern Gaza. Hamas confirmed the Israeli
airstrike overnight, calling it a "cowardly assassination." NPR's Learn Fair reports.
The Israeli military released grainy black-and-white aerial footage of a man walking
alone on a street lined with what looked like tents, then an explosion and debris.
It identified the target as Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Yunus. Hamas confirms he was one
of its senior commanders, a member of the organization's military wing since 1991.
Hamas says he helped plan and supervise the October 7 attacks,
and pledged that his "blood shall not be in vain."
Since those 2023 attacks and the Israeli assault on Gaza that followed,
health officials say Israeli attacks have killed more than 74,000 people in Gaza.
Lauren Fryer, NPR News, Tel Aviv. This is NPR.
Singapore tech company MegaSpeed says a former executive suspected of spying for China left
the company in August of last year. The company, which buys Nvidia's AI chips, tells NPR that Alice
Huang has no current role and that outside lawyers are conducting an internal investigation.
Her reported affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang helped lead to his resignation last week.
China denies spying allegations.
NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is about to achieve a major long-distance milestone.
NPR's John Stoleness has more.
It's already flown farther from Earth than any man-made spacecraft ever,
but at just after 5 a.m. Eastern time on Wednesday,
Voyager 1 will have traveled one light day away from Earth.
That's about 16 billion miles, or the distance light travels in 24 hours.
Voyager 1 launched with its twin, Voyager 2, in 1977, and traveling at almost 38,000 miles an hour,
discovered new moons and rings around both Jupiter and Saturn.
Voyager 2 took a different route to deep space in order to visit Uranus in Neptune.
It is scheduled to reach the light-day milestone nine years from now.
John Stoleness, NPR News.
Andy Warhol's 1986 self-portrait goes up for auction on Tuesday.
People can bet on whether it will sell for more than $16 million.
The wagers are part of a new partnership between art market website ArtNet and prediction market
Kalshi.
The collaboration brings betting on auction prices into the art world.
